platform: Runtime: linux/amd64 inside the platform image, the same image the platform service runs (built by components/control/platform/Dockerfile from the pinned Python 3.12 base recorded in components/control/platform/versions.json key python_base), so this component adds no image of its own and none to pin here. The compiler is a build-only CPython environment on the author's machine: it ships no service, holds no lock and runs in no container.
docs: docs/COMPONENTS.md (the detections row); the interface contract is components/control/sigma/CONTRACT.md
why_this_file_exists: Pins the build tool that produces compiled SQL. Runtime image and mapping identities are referenced by their owning files to avoid duplicate sources of truth.
status_meaning: `experimental` is a word from docs/COMPONENTS.md section 2's validation vocabulary - implementation prepared without all conformance evidence - and it is the word CONTRACT.md's own first line uses. The runner, the compiler gate and the committed artifacts are in the tree and the base tier covers them; the component still lists four open gates in conformance.md (dedicated HTTP query-user permissions, continuous Sigma container restart, provider outage, sustained query pressure), nothing has been sent to a ClickHouse from this checkout, and no container has been started from this manifest, so `verified_on` stays null and no `validated` claim exists here.

compiler.role: Build-only. It turns a reviewed examples/sigma/<rule>.yaml into examples/sigma/compiled/<rule>.json; the runtime consumes that committed SQL and never a Sigma file or a generated query (CONTRACT.md), so a compiler version move is a reviewed rebuild of the artifacts, not a deploy step.

pysigma-backend-clickhouse.upstream_status: CONTRACT.md records the backend as testing upstream: this pin is a claim about the two compiled artifacts in this tree, never a claim of general Sigma compatibility

compiler.transitive_pins: components/control/sigma/compiler.lock - 17 hash-locked packages (counted from that file on 2026-09-10); no hash is restated here

cpython.pinned_where: prose, in the first paragraph of components/control/sigma/CONTRACT.md ('Build-only compiler: CPython 3.13.7 ...'). The lock pins packages, not the interpreter, so this is the one value in this file with no machine-readable upstream pin behind it - stated rather than hidden, because a rule that has never been rebuilt under a new interpreter has never been compiled by it.
cpython.why_not_312: the pinned backend's own package metadata requires Python >= 3.13 (docs/testing-standards.md), which is why tests/compiler never runs in the 3.12 product tier and CI gives it its own job: python-version 3.13 with the job's dependencies installed from compiler.lock under --require-hashes (.gitea/workflows/ci.yml)
cpython.moving_it: regenerate compiler.lock with the `uv pip compile ... --generate-hashes` command recorded in that file's own header, rebuild every enabled rule under the new environment (CONTRACT.md, 'Rebuilding one rule'), and move docs/testing-standards.md and the CI tier's python-version in the same PR

compiler.what_this_file_does_not_pin: no image, no digest, no tag, no artifact checksum. The compiled artifacts are reviewed files under examples/sigma/compiled/ in this checkout, and their integrity is carried inside them - sigma_runner.artifact() recomputes the SQL's digest against the artifact's own `sql_sha256` and refuses a mismatch, and the event's rule version is a prefix of its `rule_sha256` - so a pin file copying either value would be a third thing to keep in step.

runtime.artifact: local_observe/platform/sigma_runner.py, run as `python -m local_observe.platform.sigma_runner` in its own container (components/control/sigma/compose.yaml, line 6)
runtime.image: ${LO_PLATFORM_IMAGE:?...} - required with no default (compose.yaml line 3), `pull_policy: never` (line 4), `platform: linux/amd64` (line 5). The digest is the operator's to resolve and pin, exactly as components/control/rca/versions.json states for its own component; this repository builds the image and publishes no registry (docs/BUILD.md).
runtime.included_by: examples/full/compose.yaml line 29 - the only example that starts this service; examples/demo and examples/platform do not include it
runtime.one_rule_per_container: LO_SIGMA_ARTIFACT names one compiled artifact (compose.yaml line 16, bind-mounted read-only from ${LO_SIGMA_ARTIFACT_FILE} at line 48) and LO_SIGMA_CURSOR names one cursor (line 17). One rule, one resource_id, one cursor, one 2-second poll loop per container: that is a detector process, not a scheduler.
runtime.liveness: the compose healthcheck is the age of that one cursor file (compose.yaml line 50, stale past 300 s, interval 30s, timeout 5s, 3 retries, start_period 60s). `restart: unless-stopped` (line 9) is not a health signal: the runner never exits on a dependency failure.

fork.status: Unimplemented design option. The current component runs one rule per process.
fork.question: one rule pack with one cursor per rule, or one container per rule stated plainly in the row. Both are legitimate; the choice changes liveness and lock semantics, so it requires an explicit component design change.
fork.pack_cost: the healthcheck tests the mtime of the single path ${LO_SIGMA_CURSOR} names, so with N cursors the container reads healthy while any one of them is fresh and a starving rule is invisible to `docker ps`; fixing that means either reading N files in the check or gating on the worst one, which puts pack policy inside a healthcheck. `local_observe/platform/owner.py::exclusive_owner` derives its lock path from the cursor argument sigma_runner.main() passes, so N cursors become N locks held by one process or one new lock path with no precedent here, and exact-batch replay is bound per cursor.
fork.per_container_cost: zero code and no change to the healthcheck, the lock, the pending-batch replay or the read bounds - all already proven as they stand - paid in deployment instead: N containers at 256 MiB and 0.5 CPU each (lines 10-11) for N rules, N producer credentials, N cursor volumes, and a startup line per container whose `shipped` figure is 1, which is why the whole-tree number comes from the command in CONTRACT.md and never from `docker logs`.

runtime.credentials: mounted files only - LO_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD_FILE, LO_CLICKHOUSE_READ_PASSWORD_FILE, LO_PRODUCER_TOKEN_FILE; the environment carries paths and never a value, and LO_CLICKHOUSE_USER is a name and not a secret
runtime.reads: signoz_logs.distributed_logs_v2 through the runner's own ClickHouse class, bounded as CONTRACT.md states (parameterised half-open UTC nanosecond windows, 5 s execution, one million rows, 64 MiB read, 128 MiB query memory, overflow throws), plus the immutable inventory snapshot; never the operational database and never a store client
runtime.writes: one coverage event per window (firing when the window's source rows were absent, unmapped or the query failed, resolved when a complete read came back), plus a `kind='security'` finding event and the count evidence behind it when the read was complete, all through the platform's authenticated intake; and the cursor file on its own volume. The third leg - the analytical copy to the owned security_events store (security store) - is code-complete and runtime-off: no shipped writer user grants it, and the grant is a reviewer's decision recorded in that component's documents.

references.rule: The same posture components/data/query-adapter/versions.json states for itself (`restates_no_digest_or_tag: true`): one pin lives in one file and moves with a reason and a rollback line, so the two identities a deployment is read against are named below by file and key and copied into no second file.

measurement.what: The one claim a rule pack makes about itself, per notification budget: `shipped` / `measured` / `unmeasured`. sigma_runner.measurement_report() counts the compiled artifacts it was given and how many carry a false-positive count measured over a named window and population; a rule that has never been counted is `unmeasured`, which is never read as quiet.

static_facts_of_this_checkout.headline: 2 rules shipped, 2 unmeasured
static_facts_of_this_checkout.how_that_was_obtained: computed on 2026-09-10 by running the command in CONTRACT.md ('What is shipped, in one line') over those two files in the Python 3.12 base environment - a property of the tree, not an observation of a running deployment
static_facts_of_this_checkout.asserted_by_name_in: tests/test_sigma_rules.py::MeasurementHonestyTests, and restated with its date in CONTRACT.md and conformance.md

measurement.operator_surface: measurement_signal() is that report in the shape /v1/overview reads: platform/overview.py validates a complete triple whose parts sum to `shipped`, with a headline bounded to 120 characters, and serves sigma_shipped, sigma_measured, sigma_unmeasured plus a status and a provenance line. Reader and producer built (overview sigma producer, the Sigma overview signal): platform/overview_worker.py publishes the triple when its configuration names a `sigma_artifacts` directory (at most 64 compiled artifacts, any unreadable one withholds the key), and a deployment with no such key answers `unknown` with three nulls and never a healthy zero. No shipped configuration sets the key, so every deployment still reads `unknown` until an operator opts in.
measurement.not_a_health_signal: Neither the startup line nor the overview signal opens, resolves or gates anything - state.py decides what is open (incident and action state) - and the container's healthcheck stays the age of its cursor.
